correctness.rationale: For the exact symmetric Fourier cutoff, the Jacobi product gives a positive lower bound proportional to \(t^{-1/2}\exp[-\pi^2/(4t)]\sin\theta\) for the full heat-kernel derivative. The omitted harmonics are bounded uniformly in angle by \(C_c N^2\exp(-N^2t)\sin\theta\) on \(t\ge c/N\). The exponential comparison proves all-angle, all-later-time monotonicity if \(c>\pi/2\). For \(c<\pi/2\), a parity-selected near-antipodal angle yields a strictly positive alternating omitted tail of size \(N\exp(-cN)/(1+e^{2c})\), dominating the exact full derivative by a Gaussian image bound. Both parity subsequences, every time and angle quantifier, and the open endpoint convention are proved. A separate 585-assertion numerical diagnostic passed but is not used as infinite evidence.

originality.rationale: The full-kernel pointwise radial monotonicity of Alonso-Orán et al. (2018) supplies a baseline but no spectral-cutoff limit. Li (2021) bounds Fourier spectral heat operators and maximum-principle error, rather than strict interior-angular derivative signs and their sharp eventual threshold. The closest indexed published discrete Fourier-collocation finding has a distinct nonnegativity predicate only on grid nodes, includes a single Nyquist mode, and obtains a different cutoff normalization. The indexed equal-polygon heat Hessian paper is a spectral-curvature statement about sampled-point energies, not monotonicity of a truncated heat kernel. No checked result implies the asserted all-angle, all-later-time recovery law with sharp constant \(\pi/2\); historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Historical priority may lie in older approximation-theory work on unimodality of partial theta series or heat-kernel shape-preserving cutoffs not indexed under those names.
Only the leading asymptotic is established; no finite-cutoff exact threshold or higher expansion is claimed.

value.rationale: Spectral cutoff can violate the intrinsic radial unimodality of positive heat flow. A sharp global shape-fidelity recovery scale different from the natural inverse-squared cutoff diffusion time is a motivated structural answer, not a numerical sample or minor parameter variant. The theorem also gives an explicit geometric location and alternating-tail mechanism of all subcritical failures for both parity classes. This is useful for understanding when bandlimited periodic heat profiles faithfully represent a central smoothing feature.
